package ambient // import "github.com/cymondez/pangolin-framework/kernel/ambient"

Package ambient provides explicit, immutable Copy-on-Write ambient scope
variables backed by context.Context.

Each Var[T] instance owns a unique, unexported pointer key, eliminating string
key collisions and allowing packages to keep their Var[T] package-private
so external code cannot forge security or lifecycle state (such as tenant,
principal, scope binding, or unit-of-work views).

Nesting uses an immutable singly-linked frame chain stored inside
context.Context. Pushing or clearing a value derives a new context without
mutating any parent frame, sharing mutable counters, or using goroutine-local
storage (GLS). Multiple goroutines can safely derive independent nested scopes
from the same parent context concurrently.

FUNCTIONS

func ScopeResult[T any, R any](v *Var[T], ctx context.Context, val T, fn func(context.Context) (R, error)) (R, error)
    ScopeResult runs fn with a derived context carrying val for v and returns
    its typed result and error. If fn is nil, ScopeResult returns the zero value
    of R and nil.


TYPES

type Slot interface {
	Clear(context.Context) context.Context
	// Has unexported methods.
}
    Slot is implemented exclusively by *Var[T]. It allows lifecycle boundaries
    such as uow.Detach to clear registered ambient variables without accepting
    arbitrary context-rewriting hooks.

type Var[T any] struct {
	// Has unexported fields.
}
    Var is an explicit, concurrency-safe ambient scope variable bound to
    context.Context. Construct with New; the zero value is invalid for writes.

func New[T any]() *Var[T]
    New creates a Var[T] backed by a unique unexported pointer key.

func (v *Var[T]) Clear(ctx context.Context) context.Context
    Clear returns a derived context in which v has no active value (Current
    and Outer report false and Depth reports 0), without mutating ctx or any
    enclosing frame. Subsequent With calls on the returned context start a fresh
    chain at depth 1. If ctx is nil, context.Background is returned.

func (v *Var[T]) Current(ctx context.Context) (T, bool)
    Current returns the active value of v in ctx, if present.

func (v *Var[T]) Depth(ctx context.Context) int
    Depth returns the active nesting depth of v in ctx (0 when absent or
    cleared).

func (v *Var[T]) Outer(ctx context.Context) (T, bool)
    Outer returns the enclosing active value immediately outside the current
    frame of v in ctx, if both the current and enclosing frames are present.

func (v *Var[T]) Scope(ctx context.Context, val T, fn func(context.Context) error) error
    Scope runs fn with a derived context carrying val for v. Because contexts
    are immutable, the enclosing context is automatically preserved when fn
    returns or panics. If fn is nil, Scope returns nil.

func (v *Var[T]) With(ctx context.Context, val T) context.Context
    With returns a derived context that pushes val onto v's immutable
    frame chain without mutating ctx or any enclosing frame. If ctx is nil,
    context.Background is used as the parent.

Package sqlite provides the real SQLite adapter on the neutral database Port. It

session. SQLite has no engine row-level security and no engine-enforced
read-only transactions usable per operation; capabilities report that

    Capabilities is the truthful SQLite contract: no row-level security and
    no transaction-scoped read-only enforcement (the query_only PRAGMA is
    connection-scoped and would poison pooled connections). SQLite always runs
    serializable internally; the neutral Port admits only the default level so
    an explicit request is never silently downgraded.

    path or a driver DSN including parameters. MaxOpen bounds the pool; a
    memory database still needs a bounded pool large enough for any RequiresNew
    nesting, because every concurrent transaction holds its own connection.
    Memory selects a shared-cache in-memory database named after Path.

package identity // import "github.com/cymondez/pangolin-framework/security/identity"

Package identity defines the protocol-independent identity/authentication
contract, the trusted orchestration that completes and installs verified
identity, and the private context storage read by resolvers.

Verifiers are trusted, explicitly registered adapters: they verify one
credential kind and return a Result. Only the pipeline in this package validates
the result and installs identity; HTTP bodies, DTOs and custom verifiers cannot
install a principal. Unfinished challenge or pending outcomes never install a
usable authenticated principal.

CONSTANTS

const (
	BearerKind  = "bearer"
	SessionKind = "session"
	ServiceKind = "service"
)
    Credential kinds select the registered verifier. Transport adapters own
    extraction; a credential value never carries parsed identity claims.

const (
	PrincipalUser    = "user"
	PrincipalService = "service"
)
    Validated principal kinds. User and service identities stay distinct:
    a verifier for user credentials must not mint service principals.

const (
	MethodJWT     = "jwt"
	MethodService = "service"
)
    Method identifiers for framework-provided verifiers. Custom verifiers use
    their own stable, non-secret method names.

const MaxCredentialBytes = 16384
    MaxCredentialBytes bounds any single credential value accepted by the
    pipeline regardless of protocol.


VARIABLES

var (
	// ErrUnauthenticated is the fail-closed sentinel for unusable credentials.
	ErrUnauthenticated = errors.New("UNAUTHENTICATED")
	// ErrChallengeRequired reports an unfinished step-up flow (for example
	// MFA); no identity was installed.
	ErrChallengeRequired = errors.New("AUTHENTICATION_CHALLENGE_REQUIRED")
	// ErrPending reports verification awaiting out-of-band completion (for
	// example device login approval); no identity was installed.
	ErrPending = errors.New("AUTHENTICATION_PENDING")
)

FUNCTIONS

func Identity(ctx context.Context) (scope.PrincipalRef, string, bool)
    Identity reads only verified identity installed by this package's trusted
    pipeline. The tenant is a credential hint; authorization still happens in
    the tenant/scope resolvers.

func Method(ctx context.Context) (string, []string, bool)
    Method reads the immutable, non-secret authentication metadata: how the
    principal authenticated (for example "jwt" or "session") and the assurance
    factors the verifier reported. Raw tokens and secrets are never stored.


TYPES

type Challenge struct {
	ID      string
	Reason  string
	Methods []string
}
    Challenge carries the non-secret continuation metadata of an unfinished
    authentication, such as which additional methods a step-up flow requires.
    Session state and login/redirect endpoints belong to the verifying module.

type ChallengeError struct{ Challenge Challenge }
    ChallengeError reports a challenge outcome without installing identity.

func (e *ChallengeError) Error() string

func (e *ChallengeError) Unwrap() error

type Credential struct {
	Kind  string
	Value string
}
    Credential is one extracted, unverified credential.

type PendingError struct{ Challenge Challenge }
    PendingError reports an out-of-band pending outcome without installing
    identity.

func (e *PendingError) Error() string

func (e *PendingError) Unwrap() error

type Pipeline struct {
	// Has unexported fields.
}
    Pipeline is the trusted authentication orchestration: it dispatches one
    credential to the verifier registered for its kind, validates the returned
    result and installs identity under the private context key. There is no
    fallback between kinds: a credential for an unregistered or failing kind
    fails closed without trying another scheme.

func NewPipeline(verifiers ...Verifier) (*Pipeline, error)
    NewPipeline registers trusted verifiers explicitly. Duplicate, empty or
    invalid kinds are rejected at construction; registration order is irrelevant
    because dispatch is by credential kind.

func (p *Pipeline) Authenticate(ctx context.Context, bearerToken string) (context.Context, error)
    Authenticate keeps the published Bearer token entry point: it verifies one
    Authorization: Bearer value against the registered bearer verifier.

func (p *Pipeline) AuthenticateCredential(ctx context.Context, credential Credential) (context.Context, error)
    AuthenticateCredential verifies one credential and installs trusted
    identity. Verifier errors are propagated unchanged; challenge and pending
    outcomes return typed errors without installing identity, so unfinished
    flows cannot bind scopes or reuse a previous identity.

type Result struct {
	Status     Status
	Principal  scope.PrincipalRef
	Tenant     string
	Method     string
	Assurances []string
	Challenge  *Challenge
}
    Result is the verifier's completed outcome. Verifiers return results;
    only the trusted pipeline installs authenticated identity.

type Status int
    Status of a verifier result. The zero value is never authenticated.

const (
	StatusAuthenticated Status = iota + 1
	StatusChallenge
	StatusPending
)
type Verifier interface {
	// Kind must match the Credential.Kind this verifier accepts.
	Kind() string
	Verify(context.Context, Credential) (Result, error)
}
    Verifier verifies one credential kind and returns an authentication result.
    Implementations are trusted, explicitly constructor-registered adapters
    (JWT, a user session store, an API-key registry, a future OIDC or device
    login module); they never install identity themselves. The pipeline keeps
    the Principal/Tenant/Scope authority rules: the returned tenant stays a hint
    that resolvers re-verify against current membership.
